title: Empirical Confidence in Level-0 Bounded Execution
current_summary: The developer-ergonomics self-dogfood wave closed clean, and one real cross-repository consumer run (DMC-RELKEY-C0-S3B, 2026-09-27) exercised the full implement/review/correct/rereview convergence loop end to end, including a real semantic defect found and fixed. Confidence remains bounded to the paths actually exercised.
next_action: Continue real DMC-RELKEY-C0 consumer runs to broaden exercised route and failure-mode coverage before treating convergence as generally proven.
notes: Do not generalize from one convergence run to general correctness, general safety, production readiness, or arbitrary-task autonomy.

title: Execution Trust and Containment Boundary
current_summary: No Coordinator-owned or Coordinator-verified OS/environment containment boundary is currently claimed; the Workflow-Profile / Security-Capability-Policy / Assurance-Floor derivation named by the product-boundary concept is not yet built, and today's control is human-authored policy and profile only.
next_action: Revisit FTR-WFC-EXECUTION-TRUST-BOUNDARIES only when a concrete consumer or Level-1 orchestrator requires a stronger containment guarantee than supervised-caller residual risk.
notes: Provider sandbox modes (e.g. Codex --sandbox workspace-write) remain provider-owned behavior, not Coordinator-trusted.

title: Run Continuation and Recovery Operator Wiring Gap
current_summary: Charged-Hop and suspend/reconcile semantics are modeled and unit-tested in the reducer, but the production operator has no entry point that wires suspension/resume into a real Run. The 2026-09-30 self-development attempt wfc-immutable-finding-echo-fix-20260930-01 gave this a real adjacent case: a legitimate mid-Hop scope escalation left useful uncommitted work with no first-class successor-Run continuation path, and the semantic escalation was obscured in published operator state by a later mechanical dirty-state/CommitIntent preemption. Same-Run crash/reconcile recovery and this semantic successor-Run continuation gap remain two distinct mechanisms, not one.
next_action: Wire same-Run reconcile/resume, or a successor-Run continuation path for legitimate scope escalations, only when concrete evidence justifies each; do not build speculative recovery or continuation machinery ahead of need.
notes: FTR-WFC-ATOMIC-HOP-RECOVERY explicitly excludes a generic outer loop from its scope and covers only same-Run technical recovery. See docs/backlog/BUG-WFC-SCOPE-ESCALATION-CONTINUATION-GAP.adoc for the distinct semantic successor-continuation case.

title: Higher-Order Autonomous Caller Mediation Boundary
current_summary: The closed product-boundary concept names a caller-mediation boundary that becomes mandatory once a Level-1 orchestrator is autonomous (not supervised); today's residual ambient capability of a supervised caller is an accepted, explicitly named deployment risk, not a containment claim.
next_action: Design the caller-mediation boundary before any autonomous (non-supervised) Level-1 orchestrator is built or granted access to WFC.
notes: A 'cooperative caller' is defined precisely by the concept and explicitly excludes a well-behaved autonomous orchestrator.

title: Project Memory Promotion Protocol Proportionality
current_summary: The strong staged-proposal Project Memory promotion protocol (d201af5) closed the original review-boundary and Make-ordering defects but still let two concurrent `memory-promote` processes both validate and consume one reviewed proposal (773ea97, empirically 14/30 double-success). Rather than add locking or transactional exclusivity, the maintainer decided to simplify toward Git as the review/acceptance/rollback boundary (DEC-WFC-010), and that simplification has now been implemented (871ab14): the staging directory, approval marker, fingerprint binding, one-shot consumption, and `memory-promote` are gone, leaving canonical JSON plus an editable workbook, a validated non-persistent import buffer, and ordinary Git review. The concurrent-promotion gap is therefore moot rather than fixed.
next_action: Obtain independent review of the Git-backed simplification (871ab14) before treating this concern as closed; do not add locking/transaction machinery ahead of a concrete multi-user need.
notes: See DEC-WFC-010. The strong-staging implementation (aa219a6, d201af5) and its reviews (56f4a04, 773ea97) remain in Git history as reusable evidence should a future use case need multi-user delayed-approval promotion.
